questions.q: A project manager is finishing a project and the sponsor is requesting insights on benefits realization. How can the project manager calculate project outcomes value? *

o.t: Evaluate qualitative and quantitative project benefits.
Price tangible benefits and divide them by expenses.
Conduct a retrospective financial assessment.
Assess outcomes and reduce them from the budget.

questions.e: To calculate the project outcomes value, the project manager should consider both the qualitative and quantitative benefits of the project. This comprehensive approach ensures that all aspects of the project's impact are taken into account, including financial metrics, customer satisfaction, process improvements, and other non-financial benefits. Therefore, the most appropriate answer is: A. Evaluate qualitative and quantitative project benefits. This approach allows the project manager to provide a holistic view of the project's outcomes, which can then be compared against the initial objectives and expectations to determine the overall value delivered.

questions.q: A project team uses the Internal Rate of Return (IRR) occasionally to select the project projected to be most beneficial to the company. On one such occasion the IRR figures for the four projects were: Project A = 5%, Project B = 0%, Project C = 3% , Project D = 10%. Which of these projects should be selected based on these IRR figures provided? *

o.t: Project A
Project B
Project C
Project D

questions.e: The Internal Rate of Return (IRR) is a measure used to evaluate the profitability of potential investments. The higher the IRR, the more desirable the project is. Based on the IRR figures provided, the project with the highest IRR should be selected. In this case, the IRR figures are: Project A = 5% Project B = 0% Project C = 3% Project D = 10% The project with the highest IRR is Project D with an IRR of 10%. Therefore, the project that should be selected based on the IRR figures is: D. Project D

questions.q: A project team is in the process of identifying the benefits associated with two projects in order to choose the one that will deliver more business value. The task involves analyzing which project best helps the company meet its compliance and regulatory requirements, as well as improve customer satisfaction. Which of the following best describes the category of the benefits being analyzed in this task? *

o.t: Quantitative benefit
Qualitative benefit
Quality benefit
Real benefit

questions.e: In this task, the team is analyzing how well each project helps meet compliance and regulatory requirements and improve customer satisfaction. These are typically more subjective and harder to measure in numerical terms, focusing on aspects such as customer satisfaction and compliance, which are not easily quantified but are crucial for overall value. The best description of these benefits is: B. Qualitative benefit

questions.q: A large-scale, multiyear transformation project was completed as per the defined requirements and within the approved budget and schedule. The requirements were also validated and confirmed by the business. However, the post-delivery analysis of the project revealed that the project did not provide benefits as expected. What should the project manager have done to avoid this? *

o.t: Ensured the requirements were properly captured in the product backlog
Created a business strategy to assist with organizational change management
Improved the status reporting processes to highlight project results
Measured and demonstrated business value throughout the project

questions.e: To avoid the issue of the project not providing the expected benefits despite meeting requirements, budget, and schedule, the project manager should have focused on continuously measuring and demonstrating the business value throughout the project. This ensures that the project delivers not just the agreed-upon outputs but also the anticipated outcomes and benefits. D. Measured and demonstrated business value throughout the project

questions.q: A company contracts a software vendor to implement and customize a new software application and assigns a project manager to initiate and lead the project. Which of the following inputs to the project charter describes the key deliverables? *

o.t: Business case
Agreements
Project scope statement
Project schedule

questions.e: In the context of a project charter, the key deliverables are typically described in the Project Scope Statement. The project scope statement provides detailed information about what the project will produce, including the specific deliverables and their characteristics. C. Project scope statement

questions.q: After completing the project charter, the project manager sends it to the project stakeholders. What should the project manager do before starting the project planning process? *

o.t: Conduct the project's kick-off meeting.
Develop the risk register.
Create the work breakdown structure (WBS).
Obtain project charter approval.

questions.e: Before starting the project planning process, the project manager should obtain project charter approval. This approval ensures that the project charter is formally accepted by the stakeholders and provides the authority to proceed with detailed planning. D. Obtain project charter approval

questions.q: A project manager just started managing agile projects. The project manager realizes that due to the lack of a clear definition of project objectives and definition of done (DoD), their colleague's projects have had many difficulties. Sponsors keep asking for more features and the project is yet to be completed. What should the project manager do to avoid these issues? *

o.t: Arrange meetings to ensure every task to complete the project is included in the project management plan.
Convince the project sponsor to incorporate quality experts so the product can be tested and accepted as completed.
Convince the product owner to approach the team and define project objectives.
Schedule meetings with key stakeholders to build the agile project charter and set clear expectations for the project.

questions.e: To avoid issues related to unclear project objectives and the definition of done (DoD), the project manager should: D. Schedule meetings with key stakeholders to build the agile project charter and set clear expectations for the project. This approach ensures that all stakeholders have a shared understanding of the project objectives, the definition of done, and expectations, which helps prevent scope creep and ensures that the project stays on track.

questions.q: A team member who is unfamiliar with the subject matter is struggling to complete a complex deliverable. What should the agile project manager do to ensure that the team member is able to take on a similar challenge in the future? *

o.t: Ensure that the team member receives adequate training and is comfortable with the subject matter.
Encourage the team member to take on more stories on this subject matter until they are completely comfortable.
Ask the team member to avoid taking on stories on this subject matter until the person is comfortable with the subject matter.
Replace the team member with a more experienced team member who will improve the team's velocity.

questions.e: To ensure that the team member can handle similar challenges in the future, the agile project manager should: A. Ensure that the team member receives adequate training and is comfortable with the subject matter. Providing training helps build the necessary skills and confidence in the team member, enabling them to successfully take on complex deliverables in the future.

questions.q: A lengthy, ongoing project exhausts a project team. Due to deadline issues, the project manager cannot extend the project schedule. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Review the project charter.
Provide more recognition to team members.
Discuss the situation with the team.
Request additional resources.

questions.e: Given the situation where the project team is exhausted and the project schedule cannot be extended, the project manager should: C. Discuss the situation with the team. Engaging with the team to understand their concerns and challenges can help identify potential solutions, such as adjusting work priorities or finding ways to improve efficiency, which can be crucial when extending the schedule is not an option.

questions.q: A project manager is struggling to figure out the performance of the project teams in an agile environment. For the same scope of work, team A has calculated and delivered 100 story points and team B has calculated and delivered 125 story points. Which team is performing better? *

o.t: Team A as they have calculated fewer story points than team B.
Team B as they have calculated more story points than team A.
The team that completes the most stories selected from the sprint backlog.
The team with the least amount of defects in their deliverables.

questions.e: D. The team with the least amount of defects in their deliverables is a better measure of performance because it reflects both the quantity and quality of the work produced. High-quality deliverables with fewer defects indicate better overall performance and value delivered to the customer, even if fewer story points are completed.

questions.q: A midsize project has the objective of developing an innovative product with changing requirements. Several team members are unavailable for two weeks per month during the duration of the project. The project manager realizes that the cost of quality increases substantially during those periods. However, the team velocity is stable. What should the project manager do to address this issue? *

o.t: Add resources to the team.
Expand the testing effort.
Provide cross-training.
Increase the sprint duration.

questions.e: Given the scenario where team members are frequently unavailable and the cost of quality increases during those periods, the best approach to address the issue would be: C. Provide cross-training. Here's why: Cross-training allows team members to be trained in multiple roles or skills. This can help ensure that the project team remains effective even when some members are unavailable. It also helps in reducing the impact of absences on the quality and continuity of work.

questions.q: A project manager has been on a complex project that began eight months ago. The project manager has a quality team that has been working hard, is motivated, and successful. What type of management and leadership should the project manager use at this stage? *

o.t: Empower them to improve results
Support with periodic iterations and feedback
Help with conflict resolution
Feedback, coaching, or help only when they ask for it

questions.e: Given that the quality team is already working hard, is motivated, and successful, the most appropriate approach would be: A. Empower them to improve results Here's why: Empowering the team involves giving them autonomy to make decisions and encouraging innovation. Since the team is already motivated and performing well, empowering them further can enhance their performance and foster a greater sense of ownership and accountability.

questions.q: A project's deliverables due date is approaching, but one team member's performance is negatively impacting the schedule. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Acquire a more skilled resource.
Remove the team member from the project.
Mentor the team member.
Ask the team member's line manager to provide training.

questions.e: Given that a team member's performance is negatively impacting the schedule, the most appropriate action would be: C. Mentor the team member. Here's why: Mentoring the team member involves providing guidance, support, and resources to help them improve their performance. This approach addresses the issue constructively and aims to develop the team member’s skills, which can help get the project back on track without immediately resorting to more drastic measures.

questions.q: A project is currently behind schedule when a new team member, known for their high performance, is assigned to the team. While assessing the new team member, the project manager realizes that the individual lacks training for the specific project but has the skills and relevant experience to join the team. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ensure that the team member receives training before joining the team.
Assign the new team member to critical activities under close monitoring while they receive training.
Assign the new team member to noncritical activities without close monitoring while training is provided.
Decline the addition of the new team member to the team.

questions.e: C. Assign the new team member to noncritical activities without close monitoring while training is provided can be a good choice: Noncritical Activities: Assigning the new team member to noncritical tasks minimizes the risk to the project if there are issues with their performance while they are learning. This approach ensures that the team member contributes to the project without affecting the critical path. Training: While the team member is being trained, their involvement in noncritical tasks allows them to gradually become familiar with the project's specifics without impacting the overall project schedule significantly. Close Monitoring: Not placing them under close monitoring while training helps them integrate into the team without added pressure, which can be beneficial for their confidence and effectiveness in the long run. In summary, this approach allows for both immediate contributions and gradual integration, balancing the need to address the project delay while managing the new team member's learning curve effectively.

questions.q: A project leader noticed that a new team member is demotivated and always arrives late to work, causing a delay in the deliverables. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask HR to deal with the team member's attendance, advise them to arrive on time, and remind them of the incentives at the end of the project.
Ask a senior team member to speak with the team member, share personal experiences, and find out the reasons for the performance issues.
During the daily meeting, ask all team members to arrive on time, and plan an event after working hours to celebrate the project progress.
Talk with the team member on a one-to-one basis, emphasizing the importance of teamwork and the value of each member's contributions.

questions.e: The best approach in this situation is: D. Talk with the team member on a one-to-one basis, emphasizing the importance of teamwork and the value of each member's contributions. Here’s why: Direct Communication: Addressing the issue directly with the team member provides an opportunity to understand any underlying issues affecting their motivation and punctuality. This personal interaction can help identify and resolve specific concerns that might not be visible to others. Emphasis on Teamwork: Highlighting the importance of teamwork and individual contributions helps the team member understand how their actions impact the overall project and the team. It can also foster a sense of responsibility and belonging. Tailored Solution: A one-on-one discussion allows for a personalized approach to resolving the issue, which can be more effective than generalized measures or relying solely on HR or senior team members. Other options like involving HR (A), asking a senior team member to speak with them (B), or planning an event (C) may not directly address the root cause of the problem or may not be as effective in motivating the individual and resolving punctuality issues.

questions.q: An agile project is running its fifth iteration out of 10. After the last retrospective, the team members realize that they had to work extra hours to deliver the committed work. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the team to have a lower commitment for the next iteration.
Ask for additional team members to maintain the velocity.
Conduct a focused retrospective to help the team to discover the root cause.
Implement a checkpoint in the iteration to verify if the team is on track.

questions.e: In this scenario, the most appropriate action for the project manager is: C. Conduct a focused retrospective to help the team discover the root cause. Here’s why: Root Cause Analysis: A focused retrospective allows the team to analyze why they had to work extra hours and identify the root causes of the issue. This could reveal problems related to scope, planning, or team dynamics that need to be addressed to prevent similar issues in the future. Continuous Improvement: Agile emphasizes continuous improvement. By understanding what went wrong and why, the team can make necessary adjustments to their processes and practices to improve future iterations. Team Involvement: Engaging the team in discovering the root cause fosters collaboration and ensures that any changes made are based on the team’s insights and experiences.

questions.q: A new warehouse facility is under construction. The project manager implements team development efforts such as training that will result in a lower defect ratio. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Introduce a training program.
Update the resource management plan.
Increase quality control reviews.
Add training costs to the budget.

questions.e: In the context of implementing team development efforts to achieve a lower defect ratio, the next step after introducing training is: B. Update the resource management plan. Here's why: Resource Management Plan: Updating the resource management plan ensures that the new training efforts and their implications are reflected in the overall project planning. It involves adjusting the plan to account for the new skills, potential changes in resource allocation, and the impact on the project’s schedule and costs. Integration: This step ensures that the training aligns with the project’s resource needs and addresses how the newly acquired skills will be utilized. It helps integrate the benefits of the training into the project’s broader context. While options A and D involve training directly, and option C involves quality control, updating the resource management plan is crucial for effectively integrating and managing the impact of the training within the project.

questions.q: An agile team is doing an excellent job of focusing on high-priority items and completing them in less time than required. Which key performance indicator (KPI) would best demonstrate this information to the project manager? *

o.t: The number of defects or missed requirements identified by the product owner.
The number of action items coming out of the end-of-iteration retrospective.
The number of user stories from the backlog that are completed per iteration.
The team consistently remains within the kanban board work in process limits.

questions.e: The best key performance indicator (KPI) to demonstrate that the agile team is focusing on high-priority items and completing them efficiently is: C. The number of user stories from the backlog that are completed per iteration. Here's why: Number of User Stories Completed: This KPI shows the team’s ability to deliver high-priority items from the backlog within each iteration. It directly reflects the team's efficiency and effectiveness in completing work and delivering value quickly. Focus on High-Priority Items: By measuring the number of user stories completed per iteration, the project manager can assess whether the team is working on and finishing the most important items in a timely manner.

questions.q: A large corporation is transforming itself from a predictive to agile approach. A project team with knowledge of agile practices is experiencing significant conflicts with the executives regarding the processes to be followed. How should these conflicts be resolved? *

o.t: Negotiate with the executives and agree on a process.
Train the executives on agile practices.
Include the executives in team retrospectives.
Request that the executives use agile practices.

questions.e: To address the conflicts between the project team and executives regarding agile practices, the most effective approach would be: B. Train the executives on agile practices. Here's why: Training on Agile Practices: Providing training to executives helps them understand agile methodologies, their benefits, and how they differ from traditional predictive approaches. This education can align their expectations with the agile processes and improve collaboration between the team and the executives.

questions.q: A team member approaches the project manager immediately after the end of the project meeting about his need for help to complete a late-due-date task. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ignore the team member's request, and ask for double the efforts to complete the task
Discuss the issue during the daily meeting, and decide the course of action with the team
Ask the team member to step out from the task and re-allocate the task to someone else
Ask a junior team member to help in the completion of the task on the due date

questions.e: The best course of action for the project manager in this situation would be: B. Discuss the issue during the daily meeting, and decide the course of action with the team Here's why: Collaborative Decision-Making: Discussing the issue with the entire team allows for a collaborative approach to problem-solving. The team can collectively assess the situation, determine the best course of action, and reallocate tasks or resources if needed.

questions.q: During a weekly team meeting, the project manager notices that one team member is consistently late in submitting their deliverables. What should the project manager do to address this issue? *

o.t: Discuss this with the resource personally, then escalate to the sponsor if not resolved.
Discuss this with the functional manager, then escalate to the project sponsor.
Discuss this with the functional manager, then escalate to the resource personally.
Discuss this with the resource personally, then provide support to resolve the issue.

questions.q: A company's project management office (PMO) is incorporating more adaptive technologies and has hired a new project manager with hybrid project management experience. The team is slow in adopting the new methodology and has not been updating project artifacts in a timely manner. Which action should the project manager take to improve the team's performance? *

o.t: Send an email asking all project team members to complete updates at the end of the day.
Set up a training session for all project team members.
Reach out to the functional managers for support.
Speak individually with each project team member about making the needed updates.

questions.e: In this situation, the most effective action would be: B. Set up a training session for all project team members. Here's why: Training and Development: A training session can address the root cause of the issue by ensuring that all team members understand the new methodology and the importance of timely updates. This approach helps build a common understanding and commitment to the new processes.

questions.q: A marketing team is developing ideas in order to revamp an existing product. The marketing executive reaches out to the project manager to make sure that necessary measures are in place for a successful launch. What should the project manager focus on? *

o.t: Ensuring that the scope management plan is in place to cover all related objectives.
Ensuring that the team is also focused on the overall change management plan.
Planning for regular project updates to cover the status of critical deliverables.
Determining and aligning performance indicators that will help in assessing successful delivery.

questions.e: For a successful product launch, the project manager should focus on: D. Determining and aligning performance indicators that will help in assessing successful delivery. Here’s why: Performance Indicators: Identifying and aligning performance indicators (KPIs) is crucial for measuring the success of the product launch. These indicators will help assess whether the objectives of the revamp and launch are met, ensuring that the new product aligns with market expectations and achieves desired outcomes.

questions.q: Some team members assigned to a new technology project expressed their lack of knowledge about the technology and the challenges they will face during implementation. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Due to the project due dates, replace the members with more knowledgeable staff.
Ask the team members to do some research and self-learning efforts about the technology.
Reallocate the members to work on and complete different tasks for which they have experience.
Reassure the team members that a training path is in place to learn the new technology.

questions.e: For a situation where team members lack knowledge about the technology and are concerned about implementation challenges, the project manager should: D. Reassure the team members that a training path is in place to learn the new technology. Here’s why: Training Path: Providing reassurance about a structured training path helps to address the team's concerns and builds confidence. It ensures that they have the necessary support to acquire the required skills and knowledge, which can lead to a more successful implementation of the new technology.

questions.q: While conducting a retrospective meeting, team members were surprised from the performance results of the team shared by the project lead. The team have all expressed their ignorance of the measurements and availability of the different tools in place. What should have the project lead done to avoid this situation? *

o.t: Ask the HR to explain the different performance measurement tools
Inform the team members to fill in feedback on a regular basis
Provide Team members with continuous feedback about their performance
Planning and define a clear performance measurement framework

questions.e: To avoid the situation where team members are surprised by performance results and unaware of the measurement tools and their availability, the project lead should have: D. Planning and define a clear performance measurement framework Here’s why: Clear Performance Measurement Framework: Establishing a clear framework ensures that all team members understand how their performance is measured, what tools are used, and how the results are communicated. This proactive approach helps to align expectations and avoid surprises during retrospective meetings.

questions.q: An organization just implemented agile and forms a development team where members are not co-located. The organization’s management style is known for setting clearly defined rules and objectives for team members. What should the agile project manager do to align the team to the desired outcomes? *

o.t: Arrange an in-person kick-off meeting to improve upon working relationships.
Discuss options with management that would align individual goals to project goals.
Schedule a speaker to inspire a collective vision across the team.
Foster commitment through team engagement and planning.

questions.e: To align a distributed agile team to the desired outcomes, the agile project manager should: D. Foster commitment through team engagement and planning. Here’s why: Foster Commitment Through Team Engagement and Planning: Engaging the team in planning sessions, setting shared goals, and ensuring active participation helps build a sense of ownership and commitment. This approach is crucial in agile environments, especially with distributed teams where team cohesion and alignment on objectives can be challenging.

questions.q: A project team received training on the technology involved with a project deliverable. In nine months of working on the project, several team members have been replaced. Productivity has slowed because new team members are not familiar with the technology and the project schedule is at risk of delay. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Meet with the entire team and ask existing members to train the new team members.
Negotiate an increase in budget with the project sponsor for additional training for the new team members.
Issue a change request for new team members already trained in the relevant technology.
Facilitate a workshop with a subject matter expert to familiarize team members with the technology.

questions.e: A. Meet with the entire team and ask existing members to train the new team members, this approach focuses on leveraging the existing team's knowledge to address the immediate training needs of the new members. Here's why this might be recommended: Knowledge Transfer: Existing team members who are already familiar with the technology can provide practical, hands-on training, which might be more relevant and immediately applicable compared to a more general workshop or training session. Team Cohesion: Involving the entire team in the training process can also help foster a sense of collaboration and shared responsibility. It can strengthen team bonds and ensure that all members are aligned with the project’s objectives. Cost and Time Efficiency: This approach might be more cost-effective and quicker compared to organizing a formal workshop with a subject matter expert or negotiating for additional budget and resources. If the team members are experienced and can effectively train their peers, this method can be a valuable way to get new members up to speed and enhance overall productivity.

questions.q: A project manager realizes that the team needs training on a specific technology that is required in the project. What should the project manager do to mitigate this risk? *

o.t: Assess the team's knowledge of the technology and look for recommended training options.
Contract with an expert provider to do the piece of work that uses that specific technology.
Create an item in the risk log and notify the sponsor.
Fix any training gaps as they arise during the project.

questions.e: To address the risk of the team needing training on a specific technology required for the project, the project manager should: A. Assess the team's knowledge of the technology and look for recommended training options. Here's why this is the best choice: Proactive Approach: Assessing the team's knowledge helps identify specific gaps in skills and understanding. This allows the project manager to address these gaps with targeted training, rather than dealing with problems as they arise or relying on external experts. Tailored Training: By evaluating the team's current knowledge, the project manager can find or design training programs that are most relevant to the technology in question, ensuring that the training is effective and efficient. Risk Management: This approach is proactive and aligns with effective risk management practices, ensuring that potential issues related to technology gaps are addressed before they impact the project's progress. Options like contracting with an expert provider (B) or creating a risk log item (C) might be necessary in some situations, but they do not directly address the immediate need for the team to acquire the required skills. Fixing gaps as they arise (D) is reactive and can lead to delays, making it less effective than proactively assessing and addressing training needs.

questions.q: A project manager is working on an agile project with a cross-functional team. The project manager is informed that some team members typically raise additional requirements that are not in the approved scope. What should the project manager do to address this expected behavior? *

o.t: Coach the team to manage scope using the appropriate framework.
Escalate to the sponsor and request replacement team members.
Conduct daily standup meetings with the team and stakeholders.
Explain that requirements cannot be changed without approval.

questions.e: To address the issue of team members raising additional requirements that are not in the approved scope, the project manager should: A. Coach the team to manage scope using the appropriate framework. Here’s why this is the best approach: Scope Management: Coaching the team on managing scope effectively aligns with agile principles, where scope can evolve but needs to be managed carefully. This approach helps the team understand how to handle changes and additional requirements in a structured manner, such as through the product backlog and iterative reviews. Empowerment: By coaching, the project manager helps the team learn how to balance and prioritize new requirements within the agile framework, which encourages continuous improvement and responsiveness to change. Alignment with Agile Practices: Agile methodologies embrace change and evolving requirements but require a structured approach to manage these changes. Coaching the team ensures that they understand and apply the agile framework properly to handle scope changes.

questions.q: A project manager believes that the project team could benefit from development activities to improve project performance and outcomes. The project manager decides to plan specific development activities for each team member. What should the project manager do first to ensure the success of this initiative? *

o.t: Conduct a skills assessment of the team members.
Ask the team to determine their development plans.
Distribute clear development plans to the team members.
Implement a reward system based on performance.

questions.e: To ensure the success of planning development activities for each team member, the project manager should first: A. Conduct a skills assessment of the team members. Here's why this is the best approach: Identification of Needs: Conducting a skills assessment helps identify the current strengths and areas for improvement of each team member. This ensures that the development activities are tailored to address specific gaps and enhance the team’s performance effectively. Informed Planning: With a clear understanding of the team’s skills and development needs, the project manager can design targeted development activities that are relevant and impactful. Alignment with Goals: The skills assessment helps align development activities with both individual and project goals, ensuring that the training and development efforts are strategic and beneficial.

questions.q: Working in a continuous delivery environment, a project leader notices that one of the key team members is experiencing low morale, affecting the project delivery and causing a serious delay in the project schedule. While discussing the issue with the team member, the project leader discovers the team member's attitude is because of uncertainty in relation to the performance review set of criteria. What should the project leader have done to avoid this situation? *

o.t: Explain the ground rules of the team.
Inform the team about incentives and rewards.
Share feedback and performance results.
Define the team-building strategies.

questions.e: To avoid a situation where a key team member’s low morale is due to uncertainty about performance review criteria, the project leader should have: C. Share feedback and performance results. Here’s why this approach is effective: Clarity and Transparency: Regularly sharing feedback and performance results helps ensure that team members understand how their work is being evaluated. This clarity can reduce uncertainty and anxiety related to performance reviews. Alignment: Providing feedback allows team members to align their efforts with performance expectations and goals, which can improve their morale and productivity. Ongoing Communication: Continuous communication about performance helps address any concerns early and provides opportunities for team members to seek clarification or support.

questions.q: While forming the team to work on a global project with incremental deliveries, the project leader shared the performance measurement plan with the team. Team members did not appreciate the proposed plan, as they expressed it is not realistic. What should the project leader do to ensure the team member's engagement in the implementation of the performance management plan? *

o.t: Ask the team members to abide by the plan, otherwise, they will not be properly appraised.
Include self-assessments at the start, middle, and end of the project to increase the autonomy of the team.
Ask the human resources team to deliver a presentation about the company's performance measurements.
Talk to the team member on a one-on-one basis to convince them about the benefits of the proposed plan.

questions.e: To ensure team members' engagement in the implementation of the performance management plan when they find it unrealistic, the project leader should: B. Include self-assessments at the start, middle, and end of the project to increase the autonomy of the team. Here’s why this approach is effective: Increased Engagement: Self-assessments provide team members with the opportunity to reflect on their own performance and align their efforts with the goals of the performance management plan. This involvement can increase their engagement and commitment. Autonomy and Ownership: Allowing team members to evaluate their own performance fosters a sense of ownership and responsibility for their work, making them more likely to accept and adhere to the performance management plan. Continuous Feedback: Self-assessments at multiple stages of the project ensure that feedback is ongoing and can be used to make adjustments to both performance and the management plan if needed.

questions.q: In a functional organization, a product analyst is assigned to a short-duration application development effort. The analyst expresses concerns about the task and asks the project manager to provide the support of a peer with expertise in this domain. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Recognize the analyst's concerns and reassign the task to another team member.
Enroll the analyst in a capacity-building program, and keep this analyst assigned to the task.
Ask the analyst to use skills to develop the tool, then move development to another team member.
Make sure the analyst has regular pairing meetings with the other team member throughout task execution.

questions.e: In a functional organization, if a product analyst expresses concerns about a task and requests support from a peer with domain expertise, the project manager should: D. Make sure the analyst has regular pairing meetings with the other team member throughout task execution. Here's why this approach is effective: Immediate Support and Learning: Regular pairing meetings allow the analyst to get immediate support and guidance from the more experienced peer, which helps address concerns and improve the quality of the work. Knowledge Transfer: Pairing provides an opportunity for knowledge transfer from the expert to the analyst, helping the analyst build expertise in the domain while working on the task. Collaboration: This approach fosters collaboration and ensures that the task benefits from the expertise of the more knowledgeable team member, leading to better outcomes and mitigating risks associated with the analyst’s initial lack of expertise.

questions.q: While forming a team to work on a global project, the project leader calls for an ice breaker meeting between the diverse team members. What should the project manager do to motivate the team to express their expectations? *

o.t: Ask the team members to write their expectations on post notes
Ask direct questions to each team member and wait for their responses
Inform the team members about the incentives of the project success
Start by doing a team self-assessment to increase team autonomy

questions.e: D. Start by doing a team self-assessment to increase team autonomy, it’s likely because starting with a self-assessment helps the team reflect on their strengths, weaknesses, and expectations in a structured way. This approach fosters a sense of ownership and encourages team members to be more open about their expectations and concerns, promoting a more engaged and motivated team environment.

questions.q: A team is assembled for a new project that will be using a predictive approach through requirements gathering and an agile approach for development and testing. Not everyone on the team has experience working in agile. The schedule has started slipping due to the unclear structure of the agile development approach. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation? *

o.t: Set up weekly status meetings to review team progress and regularly escalate delays.
Met with the team, allowed team members to make decisions about what to do, and established performance goals.
Established daily standup meetings to track team progress and escalate delays to stakeholders as appropriate.
Conducted routine meetings and identified team members who are under performing.

questions.e: In a situation where a team is struggling with the agile approach due to lack of experience and unclear structure, the best course of action is to ensure that the agile practices are properly implemented and understood by all team members. C. Established daily standup meetings to track team progress and escalate delays to stakeholders as appropriate is the most effective option. Daily standups are a fundamental part of Agile methodology that help the team stay aligned, identify issues early, and adapt quickly. They provide a structured way to track progress and address any obstacles that may be causing delays, ensuring that the team remains on track and any issues are addressed promptly.

questions.q: An information technology (IT) project manager was assigned a new team for a software development project in an agile environment. The project manager estimates that the project will take a certain number of days based on past experience in another organization. How should the project manager validate this assumption and properly plan and manage the project schedule? *

o.t: Conduct a survey in the organization and generate data to validate claims.
Estimate based on sprint review meetings and stakeholder input.
Study previous sprint planning meetings and the organization's project culture.
Ask the team members to estimate the number of story points and observe team velocity.

questions.e: To validate the assumption and properly plan and manage the project schedule in an agile environment, the project manager should focus on understanding the team's current capacity and velocity rather than relying solely on past experience or external data. D. Ask the team members to estimate the number of story points and observe team velocity is the best approach. This method involves the team directly in the estimation process, allowing them to provide their insights based on their current understanding of the work and their capabilities. Observing team velocity over sprints provides a realistic measure of how much work the team can handle, which helps in planning and managing the project schedule more accurately.

questions.q: The steering committee has asked a project manager experienced in agile to provide an indication of the time remaining on a medium-sized project. What tools can be used to provide this information? *

o.t: Analysis of the business requirements document
A release burndown chart
Story points for the remaining user stories
Surrogate measurements

questions.e: To provide an indication of the time remaining on a medium-sized agile project, the most appropriate tool is: B. A release burndown chart A release burndown chart visually tracks the progress of work completed versus work remaining over time. It provides a clear indication of how much work is left and how quickly the team is completing it, which helps in estimating the remaining time until project completion.

questions.q: A recently assigned project manager is working on detailing out all requirements and estimating each task required to complete the implementation of a healthcare system across three countries. The project manager needs this information to create the project schedule. What approach is the project manager using? *

o.t: Agile
Traditional
Steel Thread
Rolling Wave

questions.e: The approach the project manager is using is: B. Traditional In traditional project management, also known as predictive or waterfall, the focus is on detailing out all requirements and estimating each task before creating the project schedule. This approach relies on a comprehensive upfront planning process where the scope, schedule, and cost are defined early on.

questions.q: A project is implementing three magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) units for the main hospital. One of the MRI units has passed acceptance testing and the other two are in the build stage. The customer submits a change request to implement a fourth MRI unit. Which technique would produce the most accurate delivery estimate for the additional unit? *

o.t: Analogous
Bottom-up
Parametric
Relative

questions.e: The technique that would produce the most accurate delivery estimate for the additional unit is: B. Bottom-up Bottom-up estimation involves breaking down the new task into smaller components, estimating the cost or time for each component, and then aggregating those estimates to determine the overall estimate. This approach is more detailed and precise, especially when dealing with additional units or complex projects, because it takes into account the specifics of the new unit and how it fits into the overall project.

questions.q: An impact assessment reveals that a deliverable could be delayed by two weeks. A key resource has not been available to work on a non-critical activity due to other priorities. This could cause work overload on the other remaining resources. Since cost is a major constraint for this project, what should the project manager do immediately? *

o.t: Determine if the task has available float to meet the project end date.
Hire a temporary resource to do the job.
Consult the team and reduce the scope.
Change the resource calendar to avoid major delays.

questions.e: Given that cost is a major constraint and there is a potential delay in the deliverable, the project manager should: A. Determine if the task has available float to meet the project end date. Determining if the task has available float involves checking if there is any slack in the project schedule that allows for delays without affecting the overall project end date. This approach helps in assessing if the delay can be absorbed without additional cost or if adjustments need to be made. It is a cost-effective first step before considering more costly options like hiring additional resources or reducing scope.

questions.q: During a project schedule review meeting, the project team identified that one of the critical path activities has slipped due to external dependencies. The project schedule is now at risk. What should the project manager prioritize as the initial response to address the issue? *

o.t: Issue a change request and meet with the customer.
Rebaseline the schedule and notify the project sponsor.
Update the documentation and identify corrective actions.
Notify the customer and request that the timeline be extended.

questions.e: When a critical path activity slips and the project schedule is at risk, the project manager should prioritize: C. Update the documentation and identify corrective actions. Updating the documentation involves recording the current status, assessing the impact on the project, and detailing the corrective actions needed. Identifying corrective actions is crucial for addressing the issue and mitigating the impact on the schedule. This step helps in formulating a plan to get the project back on track before taking further steps like rebaselining the schedule or communicating with stakeholders.

questions.q: A vendor submits a high-level project schedule for a three-year project, including a detailed design-phase schedule. What does this describe? *

o.t: Rolling wave planning
Decomposition
Expert judgment
Templates

questions.e: The situation described—where a vendor submits a high-level project schedule for a three-year project, including a detailed design-phase schedule—illustrates: A. Rolling wave planning Rolling wave planning is a technique where detailed planning is done only for the near-term work while high-level planning is done for the work further out. In this case, the detailed schedule for the design phase represents the near-term work, while the high-level schedule covers the entire duration of the project.

questions.q: A member of a project team at a standup proposes altering a feature due to its popularity in the market. A different team member counters and is concerned about quality user experience regarding the feature. How can the project manager correct this issue? *

o.t: Present the product owner the option to place the request in the product backlog by giving the product owner suggestions.
Utilize a voting system and allow the team to decide which of the features’ version to apply.
Place the issue in the backlog of the sprint and allow the project team to decide at the next meeting.
Arrange a meeting to make a definitive decision that includes all stakeholders and the project team.

questions.e: A. Present the product owner the option to place the request in the product backlog by giving the product owner suggestions. This method aligns with Agile practices, where the product owner manages the product backlog and prioritizes features based on market demands and quality concerns. By placing the request in the backlog, the team can review and prioritize it according to its value and impact during regular backlog grooming sessions.

questions.q: A project manager has identified that a task on the critical path is behind schedule. The project manager thinks that additional resources will help, but higher management declined a request for the additional funding necessary to add resources. The project manager must work with the approved resources and budget. What would be the best-suited practice for the project manager to address this situation? *

o.t: Resource leveling
Crashing
Fast tracking
What-if scenario analysis

questions.e: Fast tracking is a project management technique used to shorten the project schedule without changing the project scope. It involves rearranging tasks so that they can be performed simultaneously rather than sequentially. This can help recover time lost when a project is behind schedule. Here’s how it works and why it’s suitable in the scenario: How Fast Tracking Works Identify Tasks: Determine which tasks on the critical path or in the project schedule can be overlapped. Typically, these are tasks that were originally planned to be done one after the other but can be performed concurrently. Analyze Dependencies: Assess the dependencies between tasks to ensure that overlapping them will not compromise the quality or outcome of the work. Some tasks may require the completion of a predecessor task before starting, so fast tracking is only possible when dependencies can be managed. Adjust the Schedule: Update the project schedule to reflect the new overlapping tasks. This may require revising the schedule to show parallel activities. Communicate Changes: Inform the project team and stakeholders about the new schedule and any changes in task execution. This ensures everyone is aware of the revised timeline and expectations. Why It’s Suitable In the scenario where a task on the critical path is behind schedule and additional resources cannot be added due to budget constraints: Time Recovery: Fast tracking allows the project manager to recover lost time by accelerating the project schedule through overlapping tasks. This can help bring the project back on track without needing extra funding. No Additional Costs: Unlike crashing, which involves adding more resources (and typically more cost), fast tracking doesn’t require additional funding. Instead, it focuses on re-sequencing tasks to optimize the project timeline. Effective Use of Existing Resources: Since additional resources aren’t available, fast tracking helps make the most out of the existing resources by optimizing task scheduling. Example: If Task A was originally planned to be completed before starting Task B, fast tracking might involve starting Task B before Task A is fully complete, as long as Task B can proceed without depending entirely on Task A. By implementing fast tracking, the project manager can effectively address schedule delays and help keep the project within its timeline.

questions.q: A construction project has progressed for about 18 months, and the schedule performance index (SPI) is 0.68. The project manager intends to complete the project as planned without additional cost. What should the project manager do to complete the project on time? *

o.t: Crash the schedule.
Fast track the schedule.
Reduce the project scope.
Reduce the project quality.

questions.e: Given that the Schedule Performance Index (SPI) is 0.68, the project is significantly behind schedule. To complete the project on time without incurring additional costs, the project manager should consider methods that expedite the schedule while minimizing additional expenses. Options Analysis Crash the Schedule (A): Description: Crashing involves adding additional resources to critical path activities to speed up the project. This often increases costs, which the scenario specifies should be avoided. Fast Track the Schedule (B): Description: Fast tracking involves overlapping tasks that were initially planned to be sequential. This approach can accelerate the schedule without necessarily increasing costs, as it involves re-sequencing work rather than adding new resources. Suitability: Given that the project manager wants to complete the project without additional cost, fast tracking is a suitable option. It optimizes the existing schedule by adjusting task sequences to reduce the overall project duration. Reduce the Project Scope (C): Description: Reducing the scope involves decreasing the project's deliverables or requirements. While this can help manage timelines, it results in a reduction of project objectives or quality. Suitability: This might not be desirable if the project scope is critical or non-negotiable. It does not directly address schedule acceleration without impacting project outcomes. Reduce the Project Quality (D): Description: Reducing quality involves lowering standards or deliverables, which can lead to compromised project outcomes. Suitability: This approach should be avoided as it undermines the quality of the deliverables and can have long-term negative impacts. Conclusion B. Fast track the schedule is the most appropriate action for completing the project on time without additional costs. By overlapping tasks and adjusting the schedule, the project manager can accelerate progress without the need for extra resources, aligning with the goal of finishing within the existing budget constraints.

questions.q: In a project where a third-party provider is implementing a custom solution, the project manager must ensure that the local team will have the capacity to support the solution. What should the project manager do to ensure that the local team can support the solution? *

o.t: Delegate the responsibility of supporting the custom solution to the third-party provider.
Conduct comprehensive training sessions for the local team on the new solution.
Reduce the responsibilities of the local team to minimize the need for support.
Hire additional personnel to provide ongoing support for the local team.

questions.e: To ensure that the local team can effectively support a custom solution provided by a third-party vendor, the project manager should focus on building the local team's capacity to handle the new solution. Here’s a breakdown of each option: A. Delegate the responsibility of supporting the custom solution to the third-party provider. Analysis: While the third-party provider might offer support, it's typically not ideal to fully delegate support responsibility. The local team should have the capability to manage and troubleshoot the solution to ensure long-term sustainability and reduce reliance on external parties. B. Conduct comprehensive training sessions for the local team on the new solution. Analysis: Providing comprehensive training is crucial for equipping the local team with the knowledge and skills needed to support the custom solution. Training ensures that the team understands how to operate, maintain, and troubleshoot the solution, thereby enhancing their capacity to support it effectively. C. Reduce the responsibilities of the local team to minimize the need for support. Analysis: Reducing the team’s responsibilities might not be a practical or effective solution. It could lead to gaps in overall project support and does not address the need for the team to support the new solution. D. Hire additional personnel to provide ongoing support for the local team. Analysis: Hiring additional personnel might be necessary if the local team cannot manage the support responsibilities alone. However, this approach involves additional costs and may not be the most efficient initial step if the existing team can be trained to handle the support. Conclusion B. Conduct comprehensive training sessions for the local team on the new solution is the best approach. It ensures that the local team is well-prepared to support the solution effectively by providing them with the necessary skills and knowledge, ultimately leading to better support and problem-solving capabilities.

questions.q: A company in the financial industry is kicking off a new hybrid project to be in compliance with new government regulations. The team has established a reliable velocity of 65 story points per iteration. Every iteration lasts 2 weeks. The sponsor wants to know when the project will be done if there are 1,040 story points remaining. How many months will it take to complete the project? *

o.t: 2 months
4 months
8 months
16 months

questions.e: To determine how long it will take to complete the project, follow these steps: Calculate the number of iterations needed: Total story points remaining: 1,040 Velocity per iteration: 65 story points Iterations needed = Total story points / Velocity per iteration Iterations needed = 1,040 / 65 ≈ 16 iterations Convert iterations into months: Each iteration lasts 2 weeks Total weeks = Number of iterations × Duration of each iteration Total weeks = 16 × 2 = 32 weeks Convert weeks into months: Typically, 1 month ≈ 4.33 weeks (52 weeks/year ÷ 12 months/year) Total months = Total weeks / Weeks per month Total months = 32 / 4.33 ≈ 7.39 months Given the options, rounding to the nearest whole number: C. 8 months is the most appropriate answer.

questions.q: A project team is working on determining dependencies for approximately 350 activities for an ongoing project. Which actions should the project team take to manage dependencies successfully? (Choose 2). *

o.t: Communicate the dependencies to the sponsor.
Assess and document the dependencies.
Communicate the dependencies to the customer.
Ensure that the dependencies are monitored.
Ensure you use only finish-to-start dependencies.

questions.e: To manage dependencies successfully in a project with a large number of activities, the project team should: B. Assess and document the dependencies. It's crucial to thoroughly assess and document all dependencies to understand how different activities are interconnected. This documentation helps in managing the sequence of activities and addressing potential delays or conflicts. D. Ensure that the dependencies are monitored. Continuously monitoring dependencies ensures that any changes or issues are promptly addressed, keeping the project on track and avoiding delays due to overlooked dependencies. Communicating dependencies to stakeholders (sponsor or customer) can be helpful, but it is secondary to the core actions of assessing, documenting, and monitoring the dependencies. Using only finish-to-start dependencies is not necessary or practical, as projects often require a variety of dependency types (e.g., start-to-start, finish-to-finish) to accurately reflect the real-world relationships between activities.

questions.q: A company is kicking off a new hybrid project to be in compliance with government regulations. The team has established a velocity of 50 story points per iteration. Every iteration lasts 1 week. The sponsor wants to know when the project will be done if there are 1,500 story points remaining. *

o.t: 30 weeks
15 weeks
4 weeks
1 week

questions.e: To determine the project completion time, you can use the following calculation: Determine the total number of iterations required: Total Iterations = Remaining Story Points Velocity per Iteration Total Iterations= Velocity per Iteration Remaining Story Points ​ Total Iterations = 1 , 500 story points 50 story points/iteration = 30 iterations Total Iterations= 50 story points/iteration 1,500 story points ​ =30 iterations Calculate the total duration: Given that each iteration lasts 1 week, the total duration in weeks is equal to the total number of iterations. Total Duration = 30 iterations × 1 week/iteration = 30 weeks Total Duration=30 iterations×1 week/iteration=30 weeks So, the project will be done in: A. 30 weeks

questions.q: A team has been working for two months and has consistently missed planned user stories. How should the project manager address this issue? *

o.t: Promote changing the iteration duration in order to commit as planned.
Ensure the sprint size is appropriate for the iteration duration.
Engage in recruiting a highly skilled resource to reinforce the skills.
Consider using a reward system to encourage timely delivery.

questions.e: When a team consistently misses planned user stories, it's important to address the issue in a way that targets the root cause. Here’s how each option aligns with addressing the problem: A. Promote changing the iteration duration in order to commit as planned. Not necessarily effective: Changing the iteration duration may not solve the root issue. It could just shift the problem to a different timeframe without addressing underlying issues such as workload management or scope definition. B. Ensure the sprint size is appropriate for the iteration duration. Effective: Ensuring the sprint size is appropriate for the iteration duration can help align the team's capacity with what is realistically achievable within each iteration. This helps in setting achievable goals and may improve the team’s ability to complete user stories as planned. C. Engage in recruiting a highly skilled resource to reinforce the skills. Not always practical: While adding skilled resources might help, it is not always a feasible or immediate solution and may not address the core issues related to the current team’s capacity or process inefficiencies. D. Consider using a reward system to encourage timely delivery. Not a core solution: While rewards can motivate the team, they do not address the underlying reasons for the missed user stories. They might not resolve systemic issues related to planning, scope, or process. The most appropriate action would be: B. Ensure the sprint size is appropriate for the iteration duration. This approach focuses on aligning the team’s work capacity with the iteration's timeframe, which can improve the likelihood of completing user stories as planned.

questions.q: An agile team has been struggling to keep up with the planned pace, which is frequently resulting in sprint failures. What should the project manager do to help avoid this situation in the future? *

o.t: Ask the project sponsor to approve overtime to compensate for the lack of performance while adjusting the plan.
Review the velocity of the team over the last several sprints and adjust the plan accordingly.
Replace junior team members with more experienced ones, and negotiate the project scope to compensate for the budget gap.
Switch to a Kanban approach to have better control on the planned pace by limiting work in progress.

questions.e: When an agile team is struggling to maintain the planned pace and experiencing frequent sprint failures, the project manager needs to address the issue in a way that aligns with agile principles and helps the team improve performance over the long term. Here’s an analysis of the options: A. Ask the project sponsor to approve overtime to compensate for the lack of performance while adjusting the plan. Not ideal: Overtime may address immediate performance gaps but is not a sustainable solution and can lead to burnout. Adjusting the plan without understanding the underlying issues may not solve the root causes of the problem. B. Review the velocity of the team over the last several sprints and adjust the plan accordingly. Appropriate: Reviewing the team's velocity over several sprints provides insight into their actual capacity and performance trends. Adjusting the plan based on this historical data helps in setting more realistic goals and expectations, which can improve the chances of success in future sprints. C. Replace junior team members with more experienced ones, and negotiate the project scope to compensate for the budget gap. Not always feasible or effective: Replacing team members might not be a practical or effective solution, and it doesn’t address the immediate issue of sprint failures. Negotiating scope changes might help, but it’s not a direct solution to the pacing problem. D. Switch to a Kanban approach to have better control on the planned pace by limiting work in progress. Possible but not immediately relevant: Switching to Kanban could help with managing work in progress and improving flow, but it may not address the immediate issues with sprint planning and velocity. This change requires time and adjustment. The best approach is: B. Review the velocity of the team over the last several sprints and adjust the plan accordingly. This option focuses on using historical performance data to set more realistic goals, which helps align the plan with the team’s actual capabilities and improves the chances of successfully meeting sprint objectives.

questions.q: During the planning phase, a project manager is creating the project schedule. The designated project team is finishing an unrelated project, so temporary resources are assigned to assist with planning and task duration estimation. The project team will replace the temporary resources prior to starting the project. What should the project manager do before the project schedule is finalized? *

o.t: Review the estimates with the designated team.
Check the task durations of previous projects.
Update duration estimation in the risk register.
Request approval from the project sponsor.

questions.e: In this situation, the project manager needs to ensure that the project schedule is accurate and reflects the input from the designated team who will eventually work on the project. Here’s an analysis of the options: A. Review the estimates with the designated team. Appropriate: Since the designated team will be the ones executing the project, it is crucial to review the estimates with them before finalizing the schedule. This ensures that the estimates are realistic and feasible from the perspective of the actual team members who will be performing the work. B. Check the task durations of previous projects. Helpful but not sufficient: While reviewing task durations from previous projects can provide useful historical data, it doesn’t ensure that the estimates are aligned with the actual capabilities and current context of the designated team. C. Update duration estimation in the risk register. Not directly relevant: Updating the risk register is important for managing risks but doesn’t directly address the need to validate the schedule estimates with the actual team members who will execute the project. D. Request approval from the project sponsor. Not the first step: Approval from the project sponsor is important, but it should come after ensuring that the estimates are accurate and have been validated by the team. The sponsor’s approval is based on a schedule that has been vetted by those who will execute it. The best approach is: A. Review the estimates with the designated team. This ensures that the project schedule is realistic and achievable, considering the input and insights of the team members who will ultimately be responsible for the project’s execution.

questions.q: A project manager for a US$15 million construction project must meet a specific project milestone earlier than planned because a season-long pattern of extreme weather is expected soon. The project is already over budget, and the project sponsor is not prepared to provide additional funding. Which tool or technique should the project manager use to achieve the milestone before the extreme weather begins? *

o.t: Simulation
Fast tracking
Resource smoothing
Crashing

questions.e: In this situation, the project manager needs to expedite the completion of a project milestone due to the impending extreme weather, without additional funding. Here’s an analysis of the options: A. Simulation Not suitable: Simulation involves modeling different scenarios to predict outcomes but doesn’t provide a practical solution for accelerating the schedule. B. Fast tracking Appropriate: Fast tracking involves performing tasks in parallel that were originally planned to be done sequentially. This can help to expedite the schedule without necessarily requiring additional resources. C. Resource smoothing Not suitable: Resource smoothing aims to adjust the schedule to align with resource availability while minimizing fluctuations in resource usage. It doesn’t focus on accelerating the project schedule. D. Crashing Not applicable: Crashing involves adding more resources to the project to reduce the duration of tasks, which would typically require additional funding. Since additional funding is not available, crashing is not feasible. The best approach is: B. Fast tracking This technique will help the project manager to expedite the schedule by overlapping tasks and accelerating the completion of the milestone without needing additional funds.

questions.q: In two months, there will be a delivery of project machines from a factory. The project team is in the process of performing a follow-up meeting to review the commitments and dependencies regarding these machines. Which actions should the project team take to ensure that the deliveries are properly performed by the factory? (Choose 2). *

o.t: Ensure that they track and monitor all dependencies and report at regular intervals.
Send an email to the research and development factory one week before delivery.
Specify exactly when a dependency is required and for how long this requirement holds.
Schedule a meeting with the factory regarding how the machine is going to be manufactured.
Talk to the factory employees to ascertain if they are qualified to build the machines.

questions.e: To ensure that the deliveries of project machines from the factory are properly performed, the project team should focus on tracking dependencies, specifying requirements, and maintaining communication. Here’s a breakdown of the options: A. Ensure that they track and monitor all dependencies and report at regular intervals. Appropriate: Tracking and monitoring dependencies and reporting them regularly helps to ensure that all dependencies are managed and that any issues are addressed in a timely manner. B. Send an email to the research and development factory one week before delivery. Not comprehensive: While this action might help remind the factory about the delivery, it is not sufficient on its own to ensure that all dependencies are managed properly. C. Specify exactly when a dependency is required and for how long this requirement holds. Appropriate: Clearly specifying the timing and duration of dependencies ensures that the factory is aware of the exact requirements, which helps in proper planning and execution. D. Schedule a meeting with the factory regarding how the machine is going to be manufactured. Not directly related: While understanding the manufacturing process is useful, it does not directly address ensuring that the delivery schedule and dependencies are managed. E. Talk to the factory employees to ascertain if they are qualified to build the machines. Not immediately relevant: The qualification of factory employees is important for quality but not directly related to managing delivery and dependencies. The best actions are: A. Ensure that they track and monitor all dependencies and report at regular intervals. C. Specify exactly when a dependency is required and for how long this requirement holds. These actions will help in managing dependencies effectively and ensuring that the delivery of the machines is properly executed according to the project’s requirements.

questions.q: After a system review for a nursing team, it was found that integration of the Radiology Informatics System was not delivered and should be included in the next sprint. The scrum master is organizing a Planning Poker session to estimate the effort. Who is responsible for making the estimate? *

o.t: Project team
Scrum Master
Product owner
Stakeholders

questions.e: In a Scrum framework, the project team (or development team) is responsible for making the estimates during a Planning Poker session. Here’s a breakdown of each role’s responsibilities: A. Project team: Correct. The development team is responsible for estimating the effort required for backlog items during the Planning Poker session. They provide the estimates based on their technical knowledge and experience. B. Scrum Master: The Scrum Master facilitates the session but does not provide estimates. Their role is to ensure that the process is followed correctly and to help the team with any questions or issues that arise during estimation. C. Product Owner: The Product Owner provides the details and priority of the backlog items but does not make the estimates. They clarify requirements and ensure that the backlog items are well-defined, but the actual estimation is done by the team. D. Stakeholders: Stakeholders may provide input and feedback on the project, but they do not participate in the estimation process. The estimation is done by the development team, who will be working on the tasks. Therefore, the correct answer is A. Project team.

questions.q: In an industrial plant, the owner has decided to add more capacity to the plant by installing a new machine and updating the software used in production. This capacity enlargement will occur while the plant is still functioning and producing. The software update will be accomplished using an agile approach in order to minimize risk. The machine procurement, installation, and integration will be accomplished using predictive approaches. What types of communications will the project manager have to design into the schedule management plan to ensure the project will be on schedule? *

o.t: Weekly colocated meetings with the relevant stakeholders
Biweekly written status reports from the relevant stakeholders
Weekly one-on-one meetings with each of the relevant stakeholders
Biweekly conference calls with the relevant stakeholders

questions.e: In a scenario where the project involves both agile and predictive approaches, the project manager must ensure effective communication to keep the project on schedule and address any issues promptly. The choice of communication method should be aligned with the needs for both types of approaches and the stakeholders involved. Here’s an analysis of the options: A. Weekly colocated meetings with the relevant stakeholders: While colocated meetings can be effective, they may not be feasible if stakeholders are distributed or if the project’s scale does not justify weekly face-to-face meetings. B. Biweekly written status reports from the relevant stakeholders: Written status reports can be useful for documenting progress and issues, but biweekly updates might not be frequent enough to address issues in a timely manner, especially in an agile environment where frequent updates and adjustments are common. C. Weekly one-on-one meetings with each of the relevant stakeholders: One-on-one meetings provide personalized updates and discussions but can be time-consuming and may not be efficient for large or distributed teams. D. Biweekly conference calls with the relevant stakeholders: Conference calls can facilitate regular updates and discussions, accommodating both agile and predictive approaches. Biweekly frequency ensures regular check-ins, which can be crucial for keeping track of progress and addressing any issues. Given the need to manage both agile and predictive aspects effectively, biweekly conference calls with the relevant stakeholders allow for regular communication and updates without the need for frequent face-to-face meetings or one-on-one sessions. Therefore, the best option for ensuring the project will be on schedule is D. Biweekly conference calls with the relevant stakeholders.
